subject: URGENT: A-Edge live checkout stalls + elevated error rate (client SDK parsing)
thread_text:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@aredge.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.inference.com
Cc: ops@aredge.com
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Live: Checkout stalls + errors spiking (started 08:58 PT)

Jordan — we started seeing a sharp uptick in 5xx errors and several live checkout streams stalling at token 0 around 08:58 PT. It looks like a streaming parse failure in our integration with the Redwood client SDK.

Symptoms:
- p99 latency for /generate jumped from ~180ms to ~1.8s
- error rate spiked to ~7% (was <0.3%)
- customers see partial/empty responses and session reconnects
- observed client logs show repeated "header fragment" and "KV cache mismatch" lines

I've attached a short log snippet and a proto capture. We rolled the client back to 2.1.2 earlier this morning and saw the issue diminish, then it came back after a canary of 2.1.3 at 08:45.

Attachments: [attachment: aedge_error_sample.log (text/plain)], [attachment: proto_trace_capture.txt (text/plain)]

Can you triage immediately? This is affecting a high-volume checkout window for A-Edge (US East).

—Maya
Maya Singh
SRE Lead, A-Edge Logistics

thread_text_3:
From: soojin_lee@redwood.inference.com
To: jordan_blake@redwood.inference.com, ben_carter@redwood.inference.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live: Checkout stalls + errors spiking (started 08:58 PT)

Quick triage notes — I pulled the proto_trace_capture and the SDK changelog for 2.1.3. Initial hypothesis: a race in the proto-splitter that coalesces header frames introduced a boundary condition when payloads are split across frames with trailing metadata. When that boundary aligns with our streaming parser's header reassembly window we can drop the pseudo-header block, leading to a parse error and immediate session teardown on the client.

Evidence:
- The capture shows repeated sequence: "HEADERS -> DATA (0-length) -> HEADERS-fragment" which matches the splitter regression we fixed on a branch but didn't fully deploy in the hotfix.
- Repro locally with a synthetic client at high concurrency; forwarding a repro to the eng team.

Proposed mitigation (next 60–90m):
- Hotfix: push a canary rollback of the proto-splitter patch in the runtime and the client shim to avoid reassembly assumptions (patch attached).
- Customer-side temporary mitigation: route A-Edge traffic to a fallback model variant that uses HTTP/1.1 ingests (slower but avoids the fussy header assembly) — only until canary stabilizes.

I'll prepare a minimal patch and a canary deployment plan.

—Soojin Lee
Senior SW Engineer, Runtime
